questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered a primary source of data in academic research?
options: A textbook summary
An original interview transcript
A magazine editorial
A Wikipedia article
questions.explanation: Primary sources are original documents or accounts created at the time of an event or by someone who experienced it firsthand.

questions.question_text: In the context of academic writing, what does the term 'plagiarism' specifically refer to?
options: Using too many citations in a paper
Presenting someone else's work or ideas as your own
Writing a paper that does not have a conclusion
Quoting an author with proper attribution
questions.explanation: Plagiarism is the act of using another person's intellectual property without giving them appropriate credit.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes the purpose of an annotated bibliography?
options: To list every book ever written on a subject
To provide a summary and evaluation of each cited source
To replace the main body of a research paper
To provide a list of definitions for technical terms
questions.explanation: An annotated bibliography includes a brief description or evaluation of the sources used to show their relevance to the research topic.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of a thesis statement in an academic essay?
options: To summarize the entire history of the topic
To provide a detailed biography of the author
To outline the central argument or claim of the paper
To define the formatting style of the citations
questions.explanation: A thesis statement acts as the roadmap for the paper, clearly stating the main point the author intends to support.

questions.question_text: Which citation style is most commonly used in the Social Sciences, including Business and Psychology?
options: MLA
APA
Chicago
Harvard
questions.explanation: The American Psychological Association (APA) style is the standard format for academic writing in the social and business sciences.

questions.question_text: What does 'peer-reviewed' imply regarding an academic journal article?
options: It was edited by students of the same age as the author
It was checked for plagiarism by a software program only
It was evaluated by experts in the same field before publication
It was published in a magazine intended for the general public
questions.explanation: Peer review ensures that the quality, methodology, and accuracy of research are scrutinized by subject matter experts.

questions.question_text: In academic writing, which of the following best defines 'synthesizing' sources?
options: Copying the exact words from a single author
Combining information from multiple sources to form a new argument
Listing sources in alphabetical order
Translating an article into another language
questions.explanation: Synthesis involves connecting ideas from different sources to create a broader understanding or a unique perspective.

questions.question_text: Which section of an academic research paper typically outlines the methodology used for data collection?
options: Introduction
Methodology
Appendices
Abstract
questions.explanation: The methodology section details how the study was conducted, including research design and data collection techniques.

questions.question_text: When conducting a literature review, what is the significance of identifying a 'gap' in existing research?
options: It proves the previous researchers were incompetent
It justifies the need for the new study being proposed
It suggests the topic is too broad to study
It indicates that secondary sources are unreliable
questions.explanation: Identifying a research gap shows what has not yet been addressed, providing a rationale for why a new study is necessary.

questions.question_text: What does an 'Abstract' typically contain in a research paper?
options: A comprehensive list of all used websites
A detailed account of the author's biography
A concise summary of the study's purpose, methods, and key findings
The full raw data collected during the research
questions.explanation: The abstract provides a quick overview so readers can determine if the article is relevant to their work without reading the entire paper.

questions.question_text: In academic writing, what is the role of a 'transition word'?
options: To increase the word count of the essay
To show logical relationships between ideas and improve flow
To define complex technical terms
To cite external authors
questions.explanation: Transition words (e.g., furthermore, however, consequently) connect thoughts so the writing is coherent and logical.
